blocks.text: After Bhai Taru Singh’s passing, the poem raises him above ordinary remembrance and names him greatest among the martyrs. The contrast is sharpened by the image of the Nawab suffering a hundred shoe beatings a day in the next world, while Taru Singh receives honour among the fearless dead.

The narrative then turns from martyrdom to living memory by describing the planting a flag post in memory of Bhai Taru Singh at Lahore. His shrine-like presence becomes a source of blessing, healing, and courage for those who approach it with faith.

Whosoever listened to the legend of Bhai Taru Singh, the text says, could hope for worldly aid, bodily recovery, and spiritual firmness. The enduring gift of the martyr is not only protection in crisis, but strength to keep his faith to his last breath.
